items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: I can see him more or less doing a lots of Tatum stuff

ctx.x: of course, he told me about when he was on the West Coast with Tatum. So I wondered whether, you know, his piano playing has improved a lot?

Yeah, I can see he had quite a bit of improvement. I can see him more or less doing a lots of Tatum stuff, because I guess that's because he plays alone. As I said, there's two kinds of piano players, one that is -- where you're playing single, and where you're playing with rhythm sections it's a different kind of piano play. And that might be the cause of it.

But I see a lot of variety in his playing. But in those days back there, McShann was really cooking. And I'd say he was as much an influence on Bird as the other guys who had supposedly taught him, and all that kind of stuff. First of all, McShann, by his own personality, created as a happy band. The guys were like family, and in fact, like I said, I'd pick up all the guys, go to work, and we'd all get in the car and go back home. Then we'd go in some restaurant, or some place in town.
